data.text:
Juan Ponce Enrile: The Man Who History Will Judge

My View from Afar and Up Close

Juan Ponce Enrile’s life was a long arc across the Philippine political landscape—marked by brilliance, controversy, reinvention, and survival. 

I do not judge him. I only reflect, as someone who stood close enough to see him in moments that shaped our nation.

He passed away at 4:21 p.m. on a Thursday in November 2025, at the age of 101. His daughter, Katrina Ponce Enrile, confirmed his passing. Until his final breath, he was serving as Chief Legal Counsel to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.—a role that closed the circle of a career that began under the father, Ferdinand Marcos Sr., six decades earlier.

Born on February 14, 1924, Enrile was the country’s oldest active public official. His legal mind was forged in the halls of the University of the Philippines, where he graduated cum laude in 1953, and sharpened further at Harvard Law School, where he earned his Master of Laws in 1955. These credentials were not just academic—they were the foundation of a career that would span generations.

His rise began under Marcos Sr., first as commissioner of the Bureau of Customs, then as undersecretary and acting secretary of Finance, and eventually as Justice Secretary. But it was as Defense Minister, starting in 1970, that Enrile became a central figure—both admired and feared. He was one of the architects of martial law, a period that left deep scars on the nation. That truth cannot be erased.

Yet in a dramatic turn, Enrile broke ranks with Marcos in February 1986. His defection, alongside General Fidel Ramos, helped ignite the EDSA People Power Revolution. 

I was there—manning a Manila Doctors Hospital ambulance, just ten meters away from Enrile and Ramos. The air was electric with uncertainty and hope. That moment remains etched in my memory.

After EDSA, Enrile transitioned into legislative work, eventually becoming the 21st Senate President. I met him again in 2012, during the lobbying for the Sin Tax Reform Law. He was 88 then—soft-spoken, mild-mannered, and attentive. Though he did not vote for the bill, which aimed to fund universal healthcare and reduce the burden of noncommunicable diseases, he allowed the debate to unfold. That, too, was leadership.

His later years were not without controversy. He was implicated in the PDAF scandal but was acquitted just weeks before his death. The law has spoken. Whether justice was served, only time will tell.

Enrile’s final role—serving another Marcos, this time the son—was a poetic coda to a life that mirrored the country’s political evolution. He was a constant presence, a legal luminary, a survivor of regimes.

He was born in Cagayan, an illegitimate child in a time when such a label could define a life. But Juan Ponce Enrile refused to be defined. He walked through the fire of judgment and into the halls of power, armed only with intellect, ambition, and an unyielding will.

A blue zone soul, he lived a full century—long enough to witness the rise and fall of regimes, the chaos of dictatorship, the fragile rebirth of democracy, and the slow erosion of public trust. He saw the country bend, break, and rebuild. He was there for all of it.

And yet, in the twilight of his life, while serving under another Marcos, he left without the chance to steer the son away from the shadows of the father. 

The opportunity to influence the course of history—to confront corruption in an administration many view as unparalleled in its excess—slipped away.

He departed with unfinished business. But perhaps that, too, is part of the legacy.

History will not repeat itself.
Because history remembers.
And history will judge.

- Dr Tony Leachon

data.text: Hello again, Manila! same traffic, same chaos, same energy ✨

At least five people were killed and 10 others injured after eight vehicles collided near the ‘Selfie Point’ on Pune’s Navale Bridge Thursday evening (November 13). Police said two vehicles caught fire following the crash, and the injured have been taken to nearby hospitals.

According to Pune City Police, the accident occurred within the jurisdiction of Sinhagad Police Station, on the Katraj-Dehu Road Bypass of the Pune-Bangalore Highway.

Rescue operations are currently underway, with multiple ambulances, fire tenders, and police teams deployed at the site.

DCP Sambhaji Kadam confirmed that all emergency agencies were on the spot. A traffic advisory has been issued, with the lane heading from Satara towards Mumbai shut for movement. Motorists have been advised to take the old Katraj Ghat route as an alternative.
